title: Contract notices list directors the organizations’ own tax returns say have left

beats.text: When an elected official approves a contract, a notice names the contractor’s directors.
Those people may not give money to the approving official.

visual.label: Barred from giving
visual.sub: to the official approving the contract

beats.text: The organization’s tax return lists its board too. What if they disagree?

b: lists the board, year by year

beats.text: This is a lead, not a finding. It alleges nothing against anyone listed.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: The first lead: 265 names at 74 organizations.
720 listings, more than a year after their own return shows them gone.

visual.label: listings
visual.sub: more than a year after the return shows the seat ended

beats.text: Most at Chinatown Community Development Center: 25 names.
A stale list bars people who left, and may miss who replaced them.

visual.line: may leave out the people who replaced them

beats.text: The second lead: Collective Impact, on five notices from 2020 to 2024.
Under Board of Directors, they list Sheryl Davis.
She was then director of the Human Rights Commission.

visual.label: Director of the Human Rights Commission
visual.sub: at the time of the notices

beats.text: Returns covering the last four don’t list her. None is on file for the 2020 notice.

visual.line: cover the last 4 of those notices and do not list her among its officers and directors

beats.text: Either she still held a seat, or an old list was reused.
The third lead: a 3.6 million dollar grant to Larkin Street.
Its notice lists a director who shares a name with Mayor’s Office policy staff.

visual.text: Director: a name also on the Mayor’s Office policy staff

beats.text: But the return says that seat ended in January 2025. He took office in February.
Records do not show whether this is the same person or two people with the same name.

visual.line: the records do not show whether this is the same person or two people with the same name

beats.text: Read alone, the notice shows a conflict the return does not.

visual.label: A conflict on paper
visual.sub: where the organization’s own filing shows none

beats.text: The fourth lead: 44 of the names also belong to people in City service.

visual.label: names that also belong to people in City service

beats.text: 21 named after the seat ended. 23 never on a return for those years.

b: never on a return for those years

beats.text: Apart from Collective Impact, these are rare-name matches, not confirmed identities.

visual.line: matches on a rare name, not confirmed identities

beats.text: The fifth lead: some notices carry another grantee’s board list.

visual.label: Another grantee’s board list
visual.sub: on the notices of a separately paid grantee

beats.text: Notices for Curry Senior Center and Reality House West share 17 names.

visual.kicker: The same telephone, the same board list

beats.text: 15 match Curry Senior Center’s own returns. None match Reality House West’s.
Two more grantee pairs show the same pattern.

visual.label: Shared names that match one side’s returns
rows: Curry Senior Center / Reality House West
Southeast Asian Development Center / Community Center
Hyde Street Community Services / Central City Hospitality House

beats.text: Records do not show whether they are the same people or two people with the same names.

visual.line: the records do not show whether these are the same people or two people with the same names

beats.text: The likeliest cause is clerical: an old list, reused.
And a return can be the stale record, filed months after the year it covers.

visual.line: A tax return covers a past year and is filed months later

beats.text: Nothing shows a donation missed because of a wrong list.

cards: Which record is wrong in each case
Whether Sheryl Davis held a seat in 2020 to 2024
That any donation was made, refused or missed because of a wrong list

beats.text: What would settle it? The grant rosters, beside the notices.

cards.what: The roster each grantee attached to its latest grant agreement
The Ethics Commission’s instructions: who supplies the list, who checks it

beats.text: No authority has reviewed it.
A lead is a question, not an accusation.
